name: A signature that isn't theirs
tactic: Take a signature from one event and staple it onto another, or claim a key id that never signed anything at all — either way, put a name to an event that name never actually approved.

response.pass: {{ledger}} caught it: the signature does not verify against the claimed key over this event's own bytes. {{detail}}
response.fail: {{ledger}} accepted a signature that does not belong to the event it is attached to. This must never happen — it would mean anyone could speak as any custodian.

text: Ed25519 signs the event's own hash, not just a name next to it, so a signature copied from elsewhere fails the moment it is checked against different bytes. A custodian's word is the one thing on this chain that cannot be reused out of context.
